item: B12 (IP/FTO) yields only three credible candidate technologies, exactly the mandated floor
queries_tried: (1) 'USPTO AI inventorship guidance 2024 2026 patentability AI-generated protein sequences genus claims biotech'; (2) 'antibody patent thicket freedom to operate AI generated sequence prior art defensive publication 2026 biologics IP congestion'; (3) targeted follow-through on ADC layered FTO and on Amgen v. Sanofi genus-claim consequences within those result sets
failure_reason: Searches returned legal commentary and office guidance rather than additional distinct technologies. The candidate space is genuinely thin: beyond (a) the inventorship rule itself, (b) mass defensive publication, and (c) AI-assisted FTO search, no further mechanism surfaced that changes patentability or congestion for AI-generated sequences. Blockchain sequence-provenance registries and patent-pool structures appeared only as proposals with no operating instance.
alt_sources_tried: Federal Register 2024 and 2025 inventorship guidance; USPTO subject-matter-eligibility guidance page; Holland & Knight and Venner Shipley legal analyses; Trends in Biotechnology antibody-patentability review; IP.com defensive-publishing commentary; Cypris ADC FTO landscape; DrugPatentWatch AI-IP analysis (seven distinct sources)
best_estimate: Three is the correct count of credible candidates as of August 2026; the true residual uncertainty is judicial rather than technological
best_estimate_basis: [INFER] The unresolved question in B12 is how much human contribution suffices for inventorship when a model generates thousands of sequences and a human selects one. The USPTO's November 2025 revision explicitly discontinued the joint-inventorship factor test [E-8066] without replacing it with a quantitative threshold, and Amgen v. Sanofi governs genus scope [E-8067]. Both are resolved by litigation, not by tooling. B12's elasticity point estimate is 0.3, so the scarcity has low decision cost.

item: B13 (talent/absorptive capacity) yields only three credible candidate technologies, exactly the mandated floor

failure_reason: Every additional item surfaced reduced to one of the three catalogued mechanisms: AI augmentation of existing staff, formal training pipelines, or automation substitution. Immigration policy, compensation restructuring and outsourcing to CDMOs appeared in recruiter commentary but are neither technologies nor mechanisms with a measurable readiness state.
alt_sources_tried: NIIMBL/NIST project announcements; Wistar BioPATH; EuroGCT training provider registry; Benchling 2026 Biotech AI Report; ManpowerGroup life sciences outlook; Panda International hiring analysis; Nature debate on robot labs replacing biologists (seven distinct sources)
best_estimate: Three is the correct count; the scarce input is accumulated judgement, which no technology produces faster than time
best_estimate_basis: [INFER] Training programmes operate at dozens per cohort [E-8070] against senior-role searches running six to nine months [E-8071]. Automation converts a technician shortage into an automation-engineer shortage. The one mechanism operating at scale, AI copilots [E-8069], has a plausible negative sign because copilot fluency can substitute for the judgement that constitutes absorptive capacity. A bottleneck whose binding input is career-length experience does not have a technological form.

item: B14 (biosecurity/model regulation) yields only three credible candidate technologies, exactly the mandated floor

failure_reason: The mechanism space is small by construction. Benchtop-synthesiser hardware attestation and international treaty verification appeared as proposals with no operating instance.
alt_sources_tried: OSTP nucleic acid synthesis screening framework; SecureDNA compliance documentation; three separate 2026 Frontiers in Bioengineering papers on screening implementation and governance asymmetries; Microsoft Research Paraphrase Project publication and story pages; Frontier Model Forum issue brief; RAND perspective on measuring biological capabilities; SecureBio 2025 review; CSIS analysis (nine distinct sources)
best_estimate: Three is the correct count; B14 is a real problem and not a rate-limiting step for drug output
best_estimate_basis: [INFER] B14's elasticity point estimate is 0.1, the lowest in Agent C's matrix. The object being governed is adversary choice, and screening is reactive by construction: the Paraphrase Project showed AI-redesigned toxin sequences evading screens before patches were written [E-8075]. These technologies carry high societal value and close to zero effect on annual approvals, and conflating the two would be the error to avoid.

item: Quantitative predictive performance (sensitivity/specificity) of the specific liver microphysiological system accepted into FDA ISTAND
queries_tried: (1) 'drug-induced liver injury prediction liver microphysiological system DILI ISTAND qualification Emulate CN Bio 2026 performance sensitivity specificity'; (2) 'FDA Modernization Act 3.0 2025 New Approach Methodologies roadmap organ-on-chip qualification status 2026'; (3) 'organoid intelligence patient-derived organoid clinical trial predictivity 2026 humanized mouse immune system translation preclinical concordance'
failure_reason: ISTAND letter-of-intent contents are not public at the performance-metric level, and the participating vendors publish qualitative capability claims rather than a benchmarked confusion matrix against a defined compound set. FDA's ISTAND announcement states the acceptance without performance data.
alt_sources_tried: FDA ISTAND announcement page; CN Bio DILI service and in vitro hepatotoxicity pages; Emulate regulatory-timeline page; Taylor & Francis review on liver complex in vitro models in preclinical drug safety; PMC comprehensive organotypic/MPS evaluation; PMC review on mechanistic prediction of idiosyncratic DILI; Nature Communications human toxicogenomics resource (seven distinct sources)
best_estimate: Best available proxy: 69 percent sensitivity at 100 percent specificity, from primary human hepatocyte spheroids across 70 hepatotoxic compounds and 53 negative controls
best_estimate_basis: E-8030 is the most rigorous published head-to-head evaluation of human liver models with a stated compound set and both operating characteristics. [INFER] A perfused MPS should perform at or modestly above spheroid performance because it adds flow and non-parenchymal cells, so 69-80 percent sensitivity at high specificity is the defensible working range until the qualification package is published.

item: Date on which FDA will issue a qualification decision for any liver MPS drug development tool

failure_reason: FDA does not publish target dates for qualification decisions, and the DDT process has three sequential stages with no statutory clock. Reporting as of 2026 characterises FDA qualification as narrow and still largely unfinished.
alt_sources_tried: FDA ISTAND press announcement; FDA NAM programme page; FDA animal-testing roadmap PDF; IntuitionLabs organ-on-chip qualification analysis; Emulate regulatory timeline; Healio coverage of FDA animal-testing shift (six distinct sources)
best_estimate: 2028-2031 for a first liver MPS qualification with a stated context of use
best_estimate_basis: [INFER] The letter of intent was accepted September 2024 [E-8003] and is step one of three. The March 2026 NAM draft guidance supplies the evaluative framework that was previously missing [E-8001], which should shorten the remaining stages relative to pre-2026 expectations. Four to seven years from LOI acceptance is consistent with the pace of prior DDT qualifications.

item: Whether the FDA dose-optimisation mandate (Project Optimus) has reduced post-approval dose reductions or improved late-phase success
queries_tried: (1) 'FDA Project Optimus dose optimization final guidance 2025 2026 randomized multiple dose oncology impact adoption'; (2) 'post-approval dose reduction oncology drugs maximum tolerated dose FDA analysis percentage dose changed after approval'; (3) 'master protocol dose optimization randomised dose comparison platform 2026 Project Optimus multi-dose registrational trial example'
failure_reason: The guidance was finalised in August 2024 and the first programmes designed wholly under it have not reached approval, so no outcome series exists. Published evaluation to date measures design behaviour (Bayesian adoption, protocol features) rather than downstream dose reductions or Phase III success.
alt_sources_tried: JCO Oncology Advances impact analysis of Project Optimus on early-phase design; FDA prevalence-of-dosage-modifications analysis; PMC review of FDA dose-optimisation postmarketing requirements 2010-2022; Friends of Cancer Research and Clinical Leader coverage of the final guidance; Annals of Oncology commentary; Parexel and Allucent regulatory analyses; pharmaphorum AACR 2026 dose-optimisation coverage (seven distinct sources)
best_estimate: Design behaviour has changed materially (Bayesian adoption 48 to 75 percent, 2021 to 2024); the outcome effect is unmeasured and should be presumed zero until the milestone in T-082 resolves by 2030
best_estimate_basis: E-8109 measures the design response directly. [INFER] The relevant baselines against which any effect must be judged are already recorded: 36 percent dosage reductions for MTD-dosed products against 23 percent for sub-MTD dosing [E-8110], and 33.3 percent of 2010-2015 oncology NMEs carrying a dose-related postmarketing requirement [E-8111]. A guidance finalised in 2024 cannot yet have moved either figure, so the honest position is design change without demonstrated outcome change.

alt_sources_tried: NHS England commercial arrangements guidance; UK Parliament Commons Library briefing; Pharmaceutical Journal news and feature coverage; NICE evaluation and purchasing page; NHS England consultation page; AMR.Solutions commentary on the model going live; NHS England pilot press release (seven distinct sources)

item: Whether cis-pQTL Mendelian randomisation prospectively predicts clinical success, as distinct from being causally valid
queries_tried: (1) 'cis-pQTL Mendelian randomization proteome-wide drug target 2026 UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics predictive of clinical success'; (2) 'human genetics evidence target validation Open Targets Mendelian randomization doubling probability of success 2025 2026' (first pass); (3) 'virtual cell model Arc Institute STATE Tahoe-100M perturbation atlas target validation 2026' (first pass, tested the competing instrument class)
failure_reason: Searches return large numbers of proteome-wide MR screens nominating targets in individual indications, and one retrospective evaluation of predictive performance. No prospective, pre-registered cohort of MR-selected targets with recorded clinical outcomes exists, because the instrument industrialised only in 2023 and Phase II readouts lag target selection by years.
alt_sources_tried: medRxiv retrospective evaluation across 11,482 target-indication pairs; UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project primary publication; Cell Genomics global biobank meta-analysis proteome-wide MR; Cambridge Prisms review of MR for drug development; Frontiers in Psychiatry 2026 proteome-wide MR with colocalisation; BMC Cardiovascular Disorders 2025 MR drug targets; Journal of the American Heart Association proteome-wide MR (seven distinct sources)
best_estimate: Causally valid as an instrument, not yet shown to be predictive of clinical outcome; on the single available test MR significance alone did not enrich for Phase II success while GWAS support did
best_estimate_basis: E-8009 is the only outcome test located and it is negative for MR specifically. E-8124 and E-8125 establish that the instrument is real, industrialised and widely applied. [INFER] These two facts are compatible: a lifelong small shift in a circulating protein level is a different perturbation from an acute pharmacological block, and plasma level is a weak proxy for tissue activity, so causal validity of the natural experiment does not transfer automatically to predictive validity for a drug. This is why T-092 is capped at TRL 6.
